items.title: No fair local estimate of the effect on pass rates
items.whyItMatters: Optional attendance makes attenders look better than they are (claim c3), so the existing registers cannot supply the effect for the analysis.
items.opportunity: Allocate 2027 tutorial groups to the two formats by timetable block and use the historical years only as context.

items.title: The perspective and the value of tutor time are not stated
items.whyItMatters: The investigator's constraints do not say whose costs count; valuing tutor time moves the near-peer cost from 11 to 19 units (claim c2).
items.opportunity: State the school perspective as the base case and a perspective that values tutor time in sensitivity analysis.

items.title: Feedback quality of near-peer tutors
items.whyItMatters: Near-peer tutors miss more technique errors (claim c4), which could affect later clinical examination even if the first OSCE is passed.
items.opportunity: Include calibration training in the near-peer arm and cost it.

items.title: Students who cannot attend evening near-peer sessions
items.whyItMatters: Students with caring duties or paid work may lose teaching if near-peer sessions run outside timetabled hours.
items.opportunity: Timetable near-peer sessions within the normal day and report attendance by these groups where recorded.

errorsFound: The investigator's constraints leave out the perspective of the analysis and the willingness to pay for an extra student passing; both must be set before any result is read.
reevaluation: An economic evaluation is still the right frame, but the effect must come from a fair comparison in 2027 rather than from past optional attendance.
summary: Four gaps: no fair effect estimate, an unstated perspective, tutor feedback quality and timetable equity.
